title: Add 'thermocline' rollout mode: progressive splits, shadow mirroring, and automated rollback orchestration
author: Carlos Nunez
description: Introduce a new rollout mode named 'thermocline' that provides time-decayed ramping (progressive splits), shadow mirroring for offline candidate evaluation, deterministic A/B splits with sticky prefix routing, and a self-healing rollback orchestration that reverts traffic on metric regressions. Changes span controller CRD changes, a lightweight runtime scheduler for local ramp enforcement, shadow forwarding instrumentation that preserves trace context, and an evaluator that supports custom user metrics and automated alerting. The PR also adds sample manifests, console preview endpoints, and E2E test harnesses. Motivation: simplify multi-step rollouts for tenants running models with large KV caches and sensitivity to cold-cache artifacts. Checklist: controller API, runtime split enforcement, shadow mirror plumbing, evaluator + anomaly detector, console preview, docs and samples, tests.

notes_on_implementation: Design highlights: controller stores the desired policy and stable snapshots; runtime performs local enforcement of ramp using deterministic timers to reduce control-plane churn. Mirror forwarding is best-effort and bounded by worker pool + drop metrics to protect production latency. Prefix stickiness (cache affinity) is implemented by hashing request prefixes and preserving affinity to reduce cold-cache impact during partial splits. Evaluator uses EWMA baselines and percentile windows; rollback resets weights to the last stable snapshot and escalates via SRE alerting hooks.
